title: The Open Chatroom
description:
KakaoTalk Open Chat: 'Seoul 20s-30s Money Study Group.'
Joined anonymously.

The chat window doesn't stop scrolling.
Real estate, stocks, crypto, apartment lottery applications.

choices.result_text:
Lurked for a few days. Learned market prices, picked up the jargon.

Open chats are Korea's information density in raw form.
The gap between those who knew first and those who didn't — it compounds.

'What should I do first with ₩200K/month?' you posted.
Replies came fast. Over ten of them. All different.

No right answer — but knowing other people are sweating the same thing helped.

title: This Meme Is About Me
description:
A meme is going around on X (Twitter).
'33, unemployed, ₩500K in the bank, when does Gangnam happen'

Over 60,000 retweets.
The replies are full of 'this is literally me.'

choices.result_text:
Retweeted it. Added 'this is literally me.'

Over 200 likes. Strangers pressed 'me too.'
You thought you were alone in this. We were all in the same place.

choices.text: Laugh and move on — a meme isn't reality
choices.result_text:
Laughed. Put the phone down.

You relate — but opening social media for comfort just pulls you deeper in.
Dopamine is too cheap these days.

title: Mukbang at 1 AM
description:
1 AM — hungry, out of money.
Opened YouTube. The algorithm recommends mukbang.

A YouTuber eating four bowls of black bean noodles.
Just the thumbnail makes your mouth water.

choices.text: Put on mukbang and eat cup ramen
choices.result_text:
Poured hot water into the cup ramen with mukbang running in the background. Weirdly fitting.

Some say Korea's mukbang culture was born to ease the loneliness of eating alone.
Cup ramen at 1 AM was enough for tonight.

choices.text: Turn it off and sleep — just makes you hungrier
choices.result_text:
Turned it off and closed my eyes.

Still hungry. At least I'm not hungrier.
Restraint is something you practice in small things first.

title: KakaoTalk Emoticons
description:
Someone sends an emoticon mid-conversation.
A dancing bear.

Kakao emoticons replace text in Korean conversation.
Sad, happy, comforting — this one bear handles it all.

choices.text: Buy one and reply in kind
choices.result_text:
Bought a ₩2,200 emoticon. A waving cat.

'Haha, cute,' they replied.
In this country, relationships are maintained less by words, more by emoticons — you keep learning this.

Sent 'haha same' in text.

The vibe was slightly different. Text has no warmth.
A ₩2,200 gap makes a temperature difference in relationships. Weird and also accurate.

title: Naver Café: Real Estate Study
description:
Naver Café: 'Real Estate Study Group.'
470,000 members.

One post, 200 replies.
Gangnam apartment prices, lottery win stories, property inspection logs...

This is the actual hub of Korean real estate information.

choices.result_text:
Started reading 30 minutes a day.

Three months later, you were using 'location value,' 'school zone,' 'subway proximity' without thinking.
Knowledge accumulates as fast as you're willing to read.

choices.text: Skim it and close the tab — this isn't my world yet
choices.result_text:
₩1 billion, ₩2 billion, ₩3 billion...

The numbers were too large to feel real.
The longer you stared, the more a sense of deprivation set in. Closed the tab.
